elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement for convenience during the Term.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires at least 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is required; instead, Customer must pay a termination fee.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: M&I's no-cause withdrawal right under Section 10.2 is effective only at the end of the Term; the immediate right is conditioned on regulatory, legislative, or judicial action and is not a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits convenience termination upon at least 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination for Convenience Fee equals three months of average monthly Fees, and the separate unamortized-cost and disposition-expense charges were removed.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 makes M&I's no-cause withdrawal of non-Core Services effective only at the end of the Term; immediate termination is separately conditioned on regulatory, legislative, or judicial action.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 requires M&I to provide 90 days' prior written notice for its end-of-Term withdrawal right.
